speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To help Members remember as we travel back through time, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) has prepared a handout featuring the Budgets that we have passed over these past few years.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members can also get it on the MP@SGPARL App.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The title of Chapter One is “Into Darkness”, covering the years 2020 to 2021.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It begins, as all good stories do, with the people involved being confronted with danger and overwhelming odds and where the outcome is, by no means, clear.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And if the title sounds familiar, that is because it is.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is respectfully borrowed from one of the movies of the rebooted Star Trek series, as it was so apt.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We started the 14th Parliament in August 2020, six months into the thick of the pandemic.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Things were dark and bleak at that time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We were still not fully out of lockdown.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We hit the ground running and deployed the necessary fiscal resources to combat this crisis.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We passed four Budgets in this time, building on the four at the end of the previous term – the Unity, Resilience, Solidarity and Fortitude Budgets.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Budgets of 2020 to 2021 enabled us to mount a strong public health response, secure early access to vaccines and protect both lives and livelihoods.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We provided household support measures to help families, with additional support for lower-income groups, through the Care and Support Package.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We were able to keep our air and sea ports open, and ensure an uninterrupted flow of critical supplies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Budgets of this period also gave us the fiscal firepower to be agile and adaptive throughout that unpredictable and volatile period, including: quick responses when new and more virulent strains of the virus appeared; the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package for fresh graduates and mid-career workers; financing schemes to help firms, especially small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with cash flow; sector-specific schemes to boost hard-hit sectors like aviation, tourism and our taxi and private hire car drivers; and pivoting from the Jobs Support Scheme to the Jobs Growth Incentive scheme when the worst of the pandemic was over, to encourage hiring in key growth sectors.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The financial assurance provided by the Budgets of 2020 and 2021 gave us the confidence to think beyond the immediate problems at hand and plan ahead, leading to the setting up of the Emerging Stronger Taskforce to identify key shifts arising from COVID-19 and make recommendations for Singapore’s economic strategies.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Through these Budgets, we were able to fulfil the promise to protect our lives, our jobs and our future.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We had emerged from darkness, a bit bruised and battered, but generally safe and ready to embark on our plans for re-opening and recovery, when we ran straight into global troubles.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Six days after this House passed Budget 2022, Russia invaded Ukraine.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The shock effects were immediate and widespread, rippling through the international order and the world economy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Global inflation spiked, energy and food prices went up, central banks ratcheted up interest rates – all leading to higher costs for businesses and investments.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We were confronted with the twin challenges of having to take care of Singaporeans’ immediate concerns in the new inflationary environment not seen since the Global Financial Crisis in 2008 while, at the same time, having to chart a new way forward for the longer term.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, Chapter Two is the story of Budgets 2022 to 2023, where we had to make tough choices and tread a path between two equally difficult challenges, much like Odysseus navigating the sea passage between Scylla and Charybdis in "The Odyssey".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is a movie too, but it is not out yet.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is coming out next year, directed by Christopher Nolan and starring Matt Damon.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These Budgets also saw intense debate in which the fundamental principles underpinning our fiscal policy were challenged, debated and ultimately upheld by the majority.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Support was given in the form of cash, Community Development Council Vouchers (CDC Vouchers), U-Save, and service and conservancy charges rebates, and more.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We expanded the Progressive Wage Scheme and introduced the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We launched Healthier SG to empower people to take charge of their health early with a view to better health over their lifetimes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We introduced the Enterprise Innovation Scheme to encourage firms to innovate and transform.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we committed to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 and backed this up with policy measures, including raising carbon taxes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Workers’ Party and the Progress Singapore Party did not support Budget 2022 as it included the GST increase.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In 2023, the Progress Singapore Party put forward an alternative Budget.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Opposition acknowledged the need for increased expenditure going forward but contended we could raise revenue in other ways.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, their alternative proposals were not agreed to as they would have involved a draw on Past Reserves or would not have raised sufficient revenues to close the gap.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Budgets 2022 and 2023 enabled us to chart a steady course despite competing pressures in a challenging macroeconomic environment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, it was also clear that we were on the cusp of a new era and faced a corresponding need to make major changes to suit changing times and a changing population – to redefine the new Singapore Dream and refresh our social compact.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This brings us to Chapter Three, or "Onward Together".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a production directed and written by Singaporeans themselves, and much of the action took place in this Chamber.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Budgets of 2024 and 2025 are about breathing life into the ideas co-created with Singaporeans under Forward Singapore and putting into motion our plans for a better and brighter tomorrow.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With the resources afforded under Budgets 2024 and 2025, we will be able to help Singaporeans with cost-of-living pressures; transform our economy and our enterprise ecosystem; push ahead with the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2.0; press on with our green transition and secure clean energy; make public housing more affordable, accessible and inclusive with more options for singles and seniors; deepen our human capital through all stages of life; help Singaporeans bounce back from setbacks and strengthen support for mental health; provide more support for seniors, lower-income groups and persons with disabilities; build a Singapore Made for Families; boost our sports and arts sectors; and rejuvenate our city.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Budgets 2024 and 2025 are enabling us to make important changes that will reshape Singapore in profound ways, while simultaneously providing ballast and stability in the current turbulent times.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This year is our 60th year of Independence, or SG60, and we are fortunate that we have surplus to share with all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As we commemorate this occasion, we can take quiet pride in how far we have come through the efforts of past and present generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We were recently named the world's most innovative country out of over 70 countries on the Global Innovation Scorecard.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our Gini co-efficient, after accounting for Government taxes and transfers, is at its lowest in two decades.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We continue to retain top spots globally in home ownership, the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) scores, healthy life expectancies and other important metrics.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Singapore passport is consistently ranked among the most powerful, with our little red book having access to the highest number of other countries in the world.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When we first set out on our journey as a nation in 1965, no one would have thought we would achieve such outcomes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We did not get to this point by accident or luck, but through careful long-term planning, building on the trust and cooperation between Singaporeans and the Government.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These are also the result of Budgets past and present, which have resourced and funded the policies that have enabled us to achieve these outcomes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We were able to decisively deploy these resources and come through without burdening future generations with debt, in contrast to many other countries that are still trying to find ways to lower their debt-to-GDP ratios, having accumulated significant debt in the COVID-19 years that exceeded the peaks after the Second World War.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are not in that position, thanks to the reserves, and to a prudent fiscal policy endorsed by the majority of this House.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This has enabled us to meet our spending needs, which have been growing year by year.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On this note, I would like to thank all Members for their active participation and contributions to our Budget debate and the COS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Over the past five years, the COS has worked extra hard.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This term, we had an average of over 600 cuts filed for each COS, with an average of seven hours and 45 minutes of debates per sitting day across each Budget and COS season.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is the highest volume and the longest duration compared to any previous term.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On behalf of this House, I would like to thank you for presiding over the proceedings with fairness, professionalism and patience.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are also very grateful to the Clerk of Parliament, Deputy Clerk and the other Assistant Clerks of Parliament, the Parliament Secretariat and staff, interpreters and translators, all of whom have been working tirelessly over the past fortnight to ensure that the proceedings went smoothly.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Hon Members, we have had a robust and meaningful debate over the past 12 days and I want to thank each of you for your contributions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This is what Parliament is all about – rigorous discussions, diverse perspectives and a shared commitment to Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Traditionally, the Speaker expresses his appreciation at the end of his speech.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But this year, I wish to do this first.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, thank you to all Members for your cooperation and your support in helping me ensure we had a rigorous, intense but orderly Budget debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: My gratitude also goes to the Leader of the House, Minister Indranee Rajah, and Deputy Leader, Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Likewise, I wish to appreciate my two Deputy Speakers, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Christopher de Souza, and to my dedicated Parliamentary Clerks and all support staff, whose unseen but invaluable backroom efforts ensured that proceedings went smoothly throughout this two-week period.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some of you spoke so fast – without taking a breath – that you quite literally took the breath away from our simultaneous language interpreters.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And for those who spoke in a more measured pace, the same staff told me it was, for them, a breath of fresh air!

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As we reflect on these debates, let us also remind ourselves that being succinct is a virtue.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Clarity and focus ensure that discussions are effective and engaging.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Parliament is at its best when we articulate our views clearly, when we have done our homework and when we debate with facts and reason.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Importantly, regardless of our political stripes, we must uphold mutual respect because respect is the foundation upon which meaningful discourse is built.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As Speaker, what impressed me most about this debate is how and why we disagree, and the disagreements can be as strong from the same side of the House as from across.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Paradoxically, our laws are binding not because their message is smooth and unfettered, but because they are stress-tested and subject to strong scrutiny.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And this is how our laws and our country mature.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This respectful and productive disagreement is not to be taken for granted.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This year's Budget was presented at a crucial time, a pivotal moment.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Geopolitical tensions are rising, economies are being reshaped by new forces and the future feels more uncertain than ever.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Like every other country, Singapore must brace for unpredictability and volatility.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: A recurring theme in our debate has been the call for "more".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: More support for workers and businesses, more security for families and more investment in Singapore's future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We discussed how economic growth must translate into tangible benefits.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And the Government has put forth measures to uplift our workforce through upskilling, reskilling and ensuring that our businesses, especially SMEs, remain competitive.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Members have also rightly pointed out that we must not pursue growth for its own sake but ensure that it leads to better wages, better jobs and better lives for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: At the same time, cost-of-living concerns remain a key priority.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The support measures, such as financial assistance for individuals and households and targeted relief for businesses, are a recognition of these pressures.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We heard different views of how best to sustain this support without overburdening future generations and this delicate balance will always be one we have to manage with care.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: On social policies, Members have spoken passionately about strengthening our safety nets, whether in healthcare, childcare, eldercare or retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The enhancements to MediSave and other healthcare initiatives are a step forward, but as some have rightly pointed out, policy alone is never enough.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We need strong community networks, families that look out for one another and a society where no one is left behind.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Singapore is ageing quite rapidly and the demands on our Budget can only increase.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And how we prepare for the future will define us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Beyond our domestic priorities, we must stay alive to global realities.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Global disruptions – be it in trade, technology or security – they can and they will impact Singapore significantly.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: While we may be small, we are far from powerless.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Our economic strength, our reserves, our strong defence and our unity as a people give us an edge in an increasingly unpredictable world.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As hon Member Mr Liang Eng Hwa reminded this House, 60 years ago, Singapore had very few cards to play and, if any, they were "weak" cards.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Today, we do have more and stronger cards, which we need to use them wisely and carefully, and always safeguard our national interests.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But having been in this House for 19 years, I can say this: a surplus does not mean we have infinite cards to play.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It simply means we have a few more this time round.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And that brings me to my final point: the strongest card we hold is the same one we have had for the last 60 years – our ability to adapt, to stay relevant and to navigate uncertainties with clarity and courage.
